hero.title: Modern Motion Planning and Vehicle Simulation Platform
hero.text: Plan trajectories with the Werling method, see every step of the computation with its physics and mathematics, simulate the vehicle from a kinematic model to a 24-state multibody model, and train neural surrogates that you can validate against the physics.
hero.art: Road with sampled candidate trajectories and the selected lane change

features.title: Built for engineers who need to know why

planning.title: Trajectory planning
planning.text: Werling planner in Frenet coordinates: optimal quintic and quartic polynomials, consistent costs, lazy selection, collision checking.

explain.title: Every step explained
explain.text: The trajectory inspector re-derives one planning cycle with the planner's numbers and checks the result against it.

dynamics.title: Vehicle dynamics
dynamics.text: Kinematic, single-track, double-track and multibody models with Pacejka, brush and isotropic tires, ESC, ABS and torque vectoring.

learning.title: Neural models
learning.text: Train a surrogate of the vehicle dynamics in seconds, or connect your own ONNX or HTTP model, and compare it with the physics in closed loop.

prediction.title: Prediction and safety
prediction.text: Constant-velocity, constant-acceleration and CTRV prediction, circle-based collision checking and safety metrics.

api.title: API first
api.text: REST service with OpenAPI, Python library, Docker image and a scenario library with ISO test maneuvers.

screens.title: A clear workspace
screens.inspector: Trajectory inspector: candidates, selected trajectory and the derivation of each step
screens.simulate: Simulation: key figures and signals of a closed-loop run

architecture.title: Architecture
architecture.text: The automated-driving stack runs as a graph of exchangeable components. The same library powers the REST service and this web app.

library.title: Python library vdsim
library.text: Models, planners, controllers and analysis; tested against literature values and physical laws.

service.title: REST service
service.text: FastAPI with OpenAPI 3, API keys, rate limits and Prometheus metrics; runs in Docker.

web.title: Web application
web.text: React, English and German, dark and light theme; charts on canvas, formulas with KaTeX.

api.title: Integrate in minutes
api.text: Every function of the web app is an API call. Use the REST endpoints from any language or the Python library directly.

openapi.title: API reference
openapi.text: Interactive OpenAPI documentation of every endpoint.

theory.title: Theory and review
theory.text: Model derivations, references and the technical review report.

source.title: Source code
source.text: Repository, issues and contribution guide on GitHub.
